notes.title: Client AC — Session Notes
notes.content:
CLIENT: AC
File #: 2024-0847
Frequency: Biweekly (Thursdays 5pm)

Presenting issues:
- Imposter syndrome (primary)
- Work-life boundary difficulties
- Strained relationship with father
- Perfectionism
- Sleep disturbance (secondary to work stress)

Demographics: Male, early 30s, tech executive, engaged

Session notes — March 6, 2026:

Client reports increased work stress over past month. Describes feeling "trapped between expectations" — board wants faster growth, team needs more support, fiancée wants more presence. Sleeping 4-5 hours/night (down from 6-7 reported in January).

Explored connection between imposter syndrome and overwork: "If I stop working, they'll realize I'm not as good as they think." Classic compensatory behavior. Client intellectually understands the pattern but struggles to interrupt it.

Father's health diagnosis (January) adding background anxiety. Client feels guilty about geographic distance. Also expressed frustration that father minimizes his own health — "He's doing the same thing I do — pretending everything is fine."

Progress:
- Developing awareness of perfectionist patterns ✓
- Identifying triggers for imposter thoughts ✓
- Behavioral change (setting boundaries): Minimal progress
- Sleep hygiene: Not implementing recommendations

Homework assigned:
1. Journaling exercise on self-compassion (10 min before bed)
2. Practice one "no" this week (delegating a task or declining a meeting)
3. Call father once this week — just to connect, not to fix

Risk assessment: No SI/HI. Not at clinical crisis level but trending in concerning direction. If sleep deprivation continues, will recommend psychiatry referral for possible sleep medication.

Next session: March 20, 2026

notes.title: Client RJ — Session Notes
notes.content:
CLIENT: RJ
File #: 2025-0112
Frequency: Weekly (Tuesdays 2pm)

Presenting issues:
- Generalized anxiety disorder
- Career transition stress
- Relationship concerns

Demographics: Female, late 20s, teacher (transitioning to tech)

Session notes — March 12, 2026:

Client completed coding bootcamp last month. Anxiety spiking around job search — fear of rejection, imposter feelings about entering tech without CS degree. 

Cognitive restructuring focus: Challenging thought "I'm not qualified" with evidence of bootcamp completion, project portfolio, and teaching skills (communication, patience, structure).

Relationship: Partner supportive of career change but client feels guilty about financial uncertainty during transition. Explored catastrophic thinking — "What if I never get hired?"

Progress: Good. Anxiety management techniques (breathing, grounding) being used regularly. Job application avoidance reducing — applied to 5 positions this week (up from 1 last month).

Homework:
1. Apply to 5 more positions this week
2. Anxiety journal (rating 1-10 before and after applications)
3. Practice interview questions with partner

Risk assessment: Low risk. No SI/HI. Functioning well despite anxiety.

notes.title: Client MW — Session Notes
notes.content:
CLIENT: MW
File #: 2024-0923
Frequency: Weekly (Mondays 10am)

Presenting issues:
- Co-parenting stress (primary)
- Adjustment to divorce
- Anger management
- Mild depression

Demographics: Male, 40s, divorced, works in finance, father of two (ages 7, 10)

Session notes — March 11, 2026:

Client reports improved communication with ex-wife this week. Used "I statements" during disagreement about children's screen time. De-escalated successfully for first time without raising voice.

Explored: Grief about family structure. "I never wanted to be a weekend dad." Normalized mourning of the intact family ideal while reframing: "You're not a weekend dad — you're an involved dad with a different schedule."

Co-parenting trigger identified: When ex makes unilateral decisions about kids' activities. Worked on: Choosing battles, accepting imperfection, focusing on what he CAN control.

Depression symptoms: Improving. PHQ-9 score: 8 (down from 14 at intake). Exercise helping. Social life rebuilding slowly.

Progress: Moderate. Anger episodes decreasing in frequency. Communication skills improving. Still struggling with acceptance.

Homework:
1. Gratitude journal (3 things about co-parenting that work)
2. Plan one fun activity with kids (not reactive to ex's plans)
3. Social: Accept one invitation this week

Risk assessment: Low risk. No SI/HI. Stable.

notes.title: CBT Techniques — Session Resource Notes
notes.content:
CBT Techniques Reference — Dr. Walsh's Practice

Core techniques I use regularly:

1. Cognitive Restructuring
   - Identify automatic thought → Evidence for/against → Balanced alternative
   - Best for: Perfectionism, imposter syndrome, catastrophizing
   - Handout: "Thought Record" worksheet

2. Behavioral Activation
   - Activity scheduling, pleasant activity tracking
   - Best for: Depression, withdrawal, avoidance
   - Track: Mood rating before and after activities

3. Exposure (graduated)
   - Fear hierarchy → systematic approach from least to most anxious
   - Best for: Social anxiety, phobias, avoidance behaviors
   - Key: Stay in situation until anxiety naturally decreases

4. Behavioral Experiments
   - Test predictions ("If I say no, they'll fire me" → test with low-risk situation)
   - Best for: Imposter syndrome, social anxiety, people-pleasing
   - Record: Prediction, experiment, outcome, learning

5. Sleep Hygiene Protocol
   - Consistent sleep/wake times, no screens 1hr before bed
   - Stimulus control (bed = sleep only)
   - Relaxation techniques (progressive muscle relaxation)
   - Best for: Insomnia secondary to anxiety/stress

6. Mindfulness Integration
   - Present-moment awareness exercises
   - Body scan, mindful breathing
   - Useful complement to cognitive work

notes.title: Hiking Trail Notes — Bay Area
notes.content:
Karen's Hiking Notes — Bay Area Favorites

Weekly hikes (self-care practice):

Palo Alto / Peninsula:
1. Rancho San Antonio (Los Altos) — My go-to weekday walk
   - Distance: 3-6 miles depending on loop
   - Difficulty: Easy-moderate
   - Best for: Quick after-work reset

2. Windy Hill (Portola Valley)
   - Distance: 7 miles (full loop)
   - Difficulty: Moderate (steep sections)
   - Views: Incredible bay views on clear days

3. Russian Ridge (Palo Alto)
   - Distance: 4-8 miles
   - Difficulty: Easy-moderate
   - Best season: Spring (wildflowers!)

Bigger adventures:
4. Muir Woods → Dipsea Steps → Stinson Beach
   - Distance: 7 miles (point to point)
   - Difficulty: Moderate-hard
   - Need: Car shuttle or Uber back

5. Point Reyes (Tomales Point)
   - Distance: 9 miles round trip
   - Difficulty: Moderate
   - Highlights: Tule elk, ocean views

Hiking schedule: Wednesday mornings (late start at office) and Sunday mornings
Hiking group: Sometimes with colleague Dr. Lisa Chen (different person from client network)

Self-care value: Essential for my own mental health. Therapists need therapy too — hiking is mine.
